newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks slide in cautious London trading.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks slide in cautious London trading.

text.p: Japanese stocks fell in cautious London trading on Thursday, as gloom over the ailing Japanese economy spread to London after sending the Tokyo market to its lowest close this year.
At 1615 GMT the Nikkei 50 index was down 21.13 points or 1.48 percent at 1404.36, after the Nikkei 225 closed at 19,570.67, its lowest since December 21 1995.
"The market closed bearish in Japan, and basically the theme just carried across to London," said one trader.
Dealers said they had seen sellers in most stocks but hardly any buyers.

"There's been a lot of caution in the market," said one trader. "I haven't seen one buyer around today. The damage was done in Tokyo, and the fall overnight made pricing difficult in London this morning."
A third trader said there was negative sentiment in the market as concern mounted over the weak Japanese economy. He saw the downward trend continuing in the last trading days of 1996.
"It's not going to recover this year," he said.
Official Japanese figures released earlier predicted a slowing in GDP growth and highlighted an economy struggling to hit its stride despite low interest rates.
